old: Its name literally describes what happens to the animals inside, via a French verb for bringing something down.
The word's root, abattre, means "to slaughter," and -oir simply marks the place where that happens.
It shares a root with the English word abate — both come from the French verb abattre.
clues: This kind of industrial building borrowed its name from French, where a suffix meaning "place for" was attached to a verb describing exactly what happens inside.
It is a facility where livestock are killed and prepared for meat; think of a more formal, French-sounding word than slaughterhouse. It has meant this ever since its coinage.
Its French parent verb, meaning "to slaughter," also gave English the word abate, as in a storm that slowly abates.
